Breastplate of Righteousness
BREST-playt of RY-chus-nes
n. phrase
Greek thōrax tēs dikaiosunēs, the second piece of the armor of God in Ephesians 6:14; drawn from Isaiah 59:17 where the LORD put on righteousness as a breastplate in His own divine-warrior armor.

See also: Breastplate of Righteousness

📖 Biblical Definition

The Breastplate of Righteousness is the second piece of the armor of God in Ephesians 6:14: stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness. Several structural features mark the doctrine. First, the breastplate’s function: it protected the vital organs of the chest (the heart particularly) in ancient combat. A blow to the head was countered by the helmet; a blow to the chest by the breastplate; together they protected the most vital body parts on which the soldier’s life depended. Second, the symbolic substance: the breastplate is righteousness. The heart of the believer—his deepest moral center, his standing-and-character before God—is protected by righteousness. Third, the question of which righteousness. The text does not explicitly specify, and the orthodox tradition has variously understood the breastplate as: (a) the imputed righteousness of Christ by which the believer is justified before God (the Reformation reading, emphasizing the objective gospel-righteousness); (b) the practical righteousness of the believer’s walk produced by the Spirit (the Wesleyan-leaning reading, emphasizing the subjective transformed life); (c) both together, with the imputed righteousness as the foundation and the practical righteousness as the consequent visible armor. The 1 Thessalonians 5:8 parallel (putting on the breastplate of faith and love) suggests that the practical-relational dimension belongs to the breastplate as well, supporting the both-together reading. Fourth, the LORD’s own breastplate (Isa 59:17): like the helmet, the breastplate-imagery is drawn from the LORD’s own divine-warrior armor. The believer wears the breastplate derivatively, by being clothed with the LORD’s righteousness through union with Christ. Fifth, the relation to the other armor: the breastplate stands between the girdle of truth (Eph 6:14, first) and the shoes of the gospel of peace (Eph 6:15, third). The truth that girds the loins is foundational; the righteousness that armors the chest is structurally next; the gospel-peace that shod the feet enables the standing-and-walking. Sixth, the practical pastoral application. The believer in spiritual warfare faces accusations against his righteousness from both directions: the adversary’s false accusations (the accuser of the brethren, Rev 12:10), and the legitimate convictions of his own conscience over actual sin. The breastplate addresses both. Against false accusations, the believer’s imputed righteousness in Christ stands firm: he is righteous because Christ is righteous and that righteousness has been credited to him. Against legitimate convictions of actual sin, the believer applies the same gospel: the blood of Christ cleanses from all sin (1 John 1:7-9); the saint confesses, is forgiven, walks in the renewed righteousness of the gospel. Both fronts are addressed by the same Christ-given righteousness, which the breastplate’s armor-protection comprehends.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 treats BREASTPLATE as defensive armor for the chest; in scripture, the Breastplate of Righteousness (Eph 6:14) is the second piece of the armor of God, protecting the believer’s heart-and-vital-organs in spiritual warfare by the Christ-given righteousness (imputed and applied) that withstands both false accusations and legitimate convictions.

BREASTPLATE, n. — 1. Armor for the breast. 2. In scripture, the breastplate of judgment of the high priest’s ephod (see separate entry) and the Breastplate of Righteousness of the armor of God (Eph 6:14).

RIGHTEOUSNESS, n. — Purity of heart and rectitude of life; conformity of heart and life to the divine law. In scripture, both the imputed righteousness of Christ by which the believer is justified, and the practical righteousness of the Spirit-wrought transformed life.

📖 Key Scripture

Ephesians 6:14 — "Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness."

1 Thessalonians 5:8 — "But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation."

Isaiah 59:17 — "For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head."

2 Corinthians 5:21 — "For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The Breastplate-of-Righteousness doctrine is corrupted, on one side, by the imputed-only reading that has divorced the breastplate from any practical-relational righteousness in the believer’s life (against the 1 Thess 5:8 parallel that adds faith and love)—and on the other by the works-only reading that has reduced the breastplate to the believer’s own moral effort without the substantive imputed-righteousness foundation that makes the practical righteousness possible.

expand to see more

The imputed-only reading divorces the breastplate from any practical-relational righteousness in the believer’s life, treating the armor-piece as exclusively the legal-forensic righteousness of justification without operative connection to the believer’s actual sanctified walk. The 1 Thessalonians 5:8 parallel refuses this. Paul there expands the breastplate to faith and love—practical-relational realities of the believer’s actual life, not merely the legal-imputed righteousness considered apart from its fruits. The both-together reading respects both texts: the breastplate’s foundation is the imputed righteousness of Christ (Eph 6:14’s undefined-but-substantive righteousness), and its practical expression is the faith and love that flow from union with Christ (1 Thess 5:8’s expansion). The recovery is the recovery of both dimensions: the believer’s heart is protected by the Christ-given righteousness in both its imputed and its applied forms.

The opposite corruption is the works-only reading that has reduced the breastplate to the believer’s own moral effort without the substantive imputed-righteousness foundation. On this reading, the breastplate protects insofar as the believer’s actual moral conduct is righteous; when his conduct fails (as it inevitably does for any honest saint), the breastplate proves inadequate and the believer is exposed to the accuser’s assaults. The Reformation insight against this is essential. The believer’s breastplate is not chiefly his own righteousness but the imputed righteousness of Christ; even when his actual conduct falls short, he stands in the perfect righteousness of Christ credited to him; the accuser’s assault on his standing is answered not by appealing to his own righteousness but by appealing to Christ’s. The practical sanctified righteousness is the fruit, not the foundation; the foundation is what the breastplate substantively is. Recover both ends. Refuse the imputed-only reading that loses the practical-relational fruit, and refuse the works-only reading that loses the imputed foundation. The biblical Breastplate of Righteousness is the Christ-given righteousness in its full scope: imputed at justification, applied through sanctification, expressed in faith and love, protecting the believer’s heart in spiritual warfare against both false accusations and legitimate convictions through the same gospel-given Christ-righteousness.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek thōrax tēs dikaiosunēs (breastplate of righteousness) from Eph 6:14; drawn from Isa 59:17 (the LORD’s divine-warrior armor); paralleled in 1 Thess 5:8 (breastplate of faith and love); the believer’s heart-and-vital-organs protection in spiritual warfare, comprehending both imputed righteousness (the foundation in Christ’s perfect righteousness credited to the believer) and applied righteousness (the practical-relational faith-and-love fruits in the believer’s sanctified life).

expand to see more

Greek thōrax (G2382) — breastplate, the armor for the chest (5 NT uses; Eph 6:14; 1 Thess 5:8; Rev 9:9, 17).

Greek dikaiosunē (G1343) — righteousness (the great NT word covering both imputed and applied righteousness).

Greek pistis (G4102) — faith (1 Thess 5:8’s addition to the breastplate).

Greek agapē (G26) — love (1 Thess 5:8’s addition to the breastplate).

Usage

"Having on the breastplate of righteousness—Paul’s instruction to wear the heart-protecting Christ-given righteousness in spiritual warfare."

"Putting on the breastplate of faith and love—1 Thess 5:8’s expansion brings the practical-relational dimension alongside the imputed foundation."

"Imputed-only reading loses the practical fruit; works-only reading loses the imputed foundation; biblical doctrine holds both as the Christ-given righteousness in its full scope."
